c.tagline: Islam's 'Porch of Mecca,' reborn after the 2004 tsunami.

taxi.fareNote: There are few metered taxis; getting around is by motorized becak, labi-labi (shared minivan), or app-based Gojek and Grab. Agree the fare before a becak or labi-labi ride. Ride-hailing apps operate in the city but cannot pick up inside the airport.

emergency.note: 112 is the nationwide emergency number connecting to police, ambulance, and fire.

avoid.reason: Aceh enforces Sharia law — dress modestly, no alcohol; unmarried couples and LGBT travellers face legal risk

hood_desc: The central district built around the iconic Baiturrahman Grand Mosque, with the main Pasar Aceh market and government offices; best for first-timers who want to be steps from the landmark and the shopping.
A busy commercial district east of the Aceh River with hotels, malls, and the main transport links; a convenient and lively base.
Banda Aceh's old Chinatown and riverside food quarter, packed with traditional coffee shops, seafood, and street stalls; best for eating and evenings out (non-alcoholic).
A coastal district with the ferry port to Pulau Weh, the tsunami memorial mosque that survived the 2004 waves, and a breezy sunset seafront; scenic and reflective.
A laid-back residential area famous for its Acehnese coffee houses, including the legendary Warung Kopi Solong; relaxed and local.

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water only.

transit.hours: Trans Koetaradja BRT buses run roughly 6:30 AM to 6:30 PM; labi-labi minivans and becak run from early morning to evening, with ride-hailing filling late-night gaps.
transit.note: Banda Aceh has no rail transit. The backbone is the Trans Koetaradja BRT network, supplemented by labi-labi (shared minivans), motorized becak, and app-based Gojek and Grab.
transit.pay: Trans Koetaradja fares are low and paid on board; labi-labi and becak fares are paid in cash and often negotiated. There is no citywide smartcard, so carry small notes.

bus: Intercity buses from Terminal Terpadu Batoh to Medan and west-coast towns
ferry: Ulee Lheue port fast ferry and slow car ferry to Pulau Weh (Sabang)
Malahayati port (Krueng Raya) for freight and regional services

transit.m: Trans Koetaradja Corridor II-A bus (airport to Pasar Aceh, ~45-60 min)
Airport taxi to city center (25-35 min); ride apps cannot pick up at the airport

tip.r: Not expected; rounding up the bill or leaving small change for good service is appreciated but not customary.

food.name: Mie Aceh
food.desc: Fat yellow noodles stir-fried or served soupy in a dark curry of cardamom, cumin and chili, topped with beef, crab or prawns and a scatter of pickle and emping.

places.name: Mie Razali
places.note: The name locals give first when asked where to eat mie Aceh; open late, always busy.

places.name: Mie Aceh Seulawah
places.note: Long-running noodle house rated highly by recent visitors for its crab version.

places.name: Rex Peunayong food street
places.note: Row of night stalls where several mie Aceh cooks work side by side after dark.

food.name: Kuah beulangong
food.desc: Beef or goat curry cooked with young jackfruit in a huge communal cauldron, thick with coconut and spice. Traditionally a feast dish for weddings and kenduri.

places.name: Rumah Makan Spesifik Aceh
places.note: Known for keeping the harder-to-find traditional Acehnese dishes on the daily counter.

places.name: Rex Peunayong food street
places.note: Evening stalls ladle beulangong from the pot; go early before the cauldron empties.

places.name: Warungs along the Lambaro road
places.note: Roadside kitchens outside the city cook the village version in the traditional big pan.

food.name: Ayam tangkap
food.desc: Chicken fried with a whole thicket of curry leaves, pandan and chili until the leaves crisp up; you eat the herbs as much as the bird.

places.name: Ayam Tangkap Hasan
places.note: The address most often cited for ayam tangkap done the classic Aceh Besar way.

places.name: Rumah Makan Spesifik Aceh
places.note: Reliable version served with rice and the usual Acehnese side sambals.

places.name: Ulee Kareng warungs
places.note: Several neighbourhood kitchens in the coffee district fry it fresh to order.

food.name: Sie reuboh
food.desc: Beef and fat slow-cooked in palm vinegar, turmeric and chili until preserved and deeply sour - an Aceh Besar farmhouse dish that predates refrigeration.

places.name: Rumah Makan Spesifik Aceh
places.note: One of the few city restaurants that keeps this old Aceh Besar speciality going.

places.name: Montasik village warungs
places.note: The home of sie reuboh; village kitchens sell it by the portion from clay pots.

places.name: Pasar Aceh food stalls
places.note: Market cooks sell sie reuboh alongside the daily rice-and-curry spread.

food.name: Kuah pliek u
food.desc: Vegetable curry built on pliek u, the fermented pressed coconut left after oil-making - funky, savoury and considered the true taste of an Acehnese village.

places.name: Rumah Makan Spesifik Aceh
places.note: Serves the fermented-coconut curry that most tourist restaurants leave off the menu.

places.name: Pasar Aceh food stalls
places.note: Cheap and authentic; the market cooks make it the way home kitchens do.

places.name: Ulee Kareng warungs
places.note: Neighbourhood nasi campur stalls usually have a tray of pliek u at lunchtime.

food.name: Roti cane with kari
food.desc: Flaky griddled flatbread pulled and slapped to order, torn and dipped into goat or chicken curry - the Indian-Acehnese breakfast of Peunayong.

places.name: Peunayong roti shops
places.note: The old trading quarter's roti cane stalls fire up from dawn and again late at night.

places.name: Canai Mamak
places.note: Popular sit-down spot for roti canai and curry with the city's coffee-shop crowd.

places.name: Mie Razali
places.note: Serves roti cane alongside the noodles if you want both in one stop.

food.name: Kopi sanger
food.desc: Aceh's own coffee: robusta strained repeatedly through a cloth sock, mixed with condensed milk and whipped to a froth. Aceh is dry, and coffee is the nightlife.

places.name: Warung Kopi Solong
places.note: The legendary Ulee Kareng coffee house, roasting its own beans for decades.

places.name: Kedai Kopi Seirama
places.note: Well-reviewed modern kopi shop turning out carefully made sanger from about IDR 20,000.

places.name: Rumoh Aceh Warung Kopi
places.note: Big, buzzing warkop where locals sit over sanger until well past midnight.

food.name: Kopi saring Aceh
food.desc: Black Gayo-highland coffee poured back and forth through a long cloth filter from height, arriving thick, bitter and faintly caramelised. Order it without milk.

places.name: Warung Kopi Solong
places.note: Watch the barista work the cloth sock at the counter - the classic Banda Aceh sight.

places.name: Warung Kopi Zakir
places.note: Old-school warkop popular with locals for straight black saring coffee and snacks.

places.name: Peunayong coffee shops
places.note: The trading quarter's kopi stalls serve saring coffee with roti from early morning.

landmarks: Baiturrahman Grand Mosque
Aceh's soul in black domes and white marble, this magnificent 19th-century mosque miraculously survived the 2004 tsunami and anchors the city.
Aceh Tsunami Museum
Ridwan Kamil's moving architectural memorial, where a dark dripping corridor and wall of names honor the 2004 disaster's victims.
PLTD Apung 1 (Floating Power Plant Ship)
A 2,600-ton generator ship hurled five kilometers inland by the tsunami, now a stark monument you can climb for city views.
Lampulo Boat on the Roof
A fishing boat stranded atop a house that saved 59 lives during the tsunami, preserved exactly where the waves left it.
Gunongan
A whimsical white 17th-century pleasure palace built by Sultan Iskandar Muda for his Malay princess, resembling a stylized mountain.
Aceh Museum and Rumoh Aceh
The provincial museum centered on a splendid traditional stilt house, displaying weaponry, manuscripts, and the great Cakra Donya bell.
Kerkhof Peucut Cemetery
The world's largest Dutch military cemetery outside the Netherlands, where 2,200 colonial-era graves recall the bitter Aceh War.
Baiturrahim Mosque, Ulee Lheue
A resilient white seafront mosque that withstood the tsunami as everything around it was swept away, now a symbol of faith.
Lampuuk Beach
A sweeping crescent of white sand and turquoise surf beneath cliffs just outside the city, beloved for sunsets and seafood shacks.
Ulee Lheue Beach and Harbor
The rebuilt waterfront esplanade where locals gather for grilled corn and sunset views, gateway to ferries for Pulau Weh's reefs.

train.note: Banda Aceh has no railway. The only working track in Aceh is a short reactivated stretch of the Trans-Sumatra line in North Aceh, between Krueng Geukueh/Krueng Mane and Bungkah, worked by the government-run Cut Meutia railbus - it is about 250 km east of the city and of no use for getting here. PT Kereta Api Indonesia's nearest real network is the North Sumatra division around Medan, where trains run to Kualanamu airport, Tebing Tinggi and Rantau Prapat (https://booking.kai.id/). The long-discussed extension of the Sumatra railway to Banda Aceh remains a plan, so arrive by bus or air.

bus.note: Long-distance buses leave Terminal Terpadu Batoh south along the east coast to Medan, North Sumatra (~12 hours), and down the quieter west coast to Meulaboh and beyond.

intl.to: Pulau Weh / Sabang (Indonesia) - from Ulee Lheue port, ~45 min fast ferry or ~2 hr car ferry

ferry.note: Fast ferries (~45 min) and a slower car ferry (~2 hours) run from Ulee Lheue port to Balohan on Pulau Weh (Sabang), the diving gateway off the northern tip of Sumatra.

half.name: Gunung Seulawah Agam
half.blurb: An active stratovolcano rising outside the city, its forested slopes popular for hiking and its crater visible from a ridge trail.

full.name: Sabang / Pulau Weh
full.blurb: An island reached by ferry from Banda Aceh, marked by Indonesia's westernmost point and clear-water dive sites around Rubiah Island.
